caveat: Approximation of what a dog's or cat's cones capture, not of what the animal subjectively experiences. Assumes sRGB input and a modelled display (Gaussian primaries); see src/prototype/README.md.

convention.space: linear sRGB (D65), matrix acts on column vectors: out = M @ rgb

pipeline: gamut fit: clamp each channel to [0, 1]

v2.description: Dog-specific projection derived from Govardovskii cone sensitivities (S 429 / L 555 nm), 475 nm anchor. Shipped default (NOTES.md, Phase 3 decision).

v0.description: Vienot, Brettel & Mollon (1999) deuteranopia matrix for linear sRGB. Fallback.

cat.description: Cat-specific projection derived from Govardovskii cone sensitivities (S 450 / L 555 nm), 475 nm anchor. Approximate: the cat parameters are not verified against primary papers.

acuity.edges: mirror preferred; clamp-to-edge is acceptable where mirroring is unavailable (external camera textures may only support clamp)
acuity.kernel: Gaussian, isotropic; truncate at 3 sigma or more
acuity.hfov_applies_to: the long edge of the frame

peripheral_blur.note: artistic; per-profile 'peripheral_blur' (0 = uniform blur). Blur grows towards the frame edges, the way acuity falls away from the centre of the retina
peripheral_blur.r2: ((x - cx)^2 + (y - cy)^2) / (cx^2 + cy^2), pixel centres, cx = (width - 1) / 2, cy = (height - 1) / 2: 0 at the frame centre, 1 in the corners
peripheral_blur.reference_implementation: acuity.peripheral_blur blends 5 uniform Gaussian blurs evenly spaced in r2 with linear weights; a shader may evaluate the Gaussian per pixel instead

linear_light_check.note: a 50/50 black-white checker blurred to a flat value encodes to this sRGB value

shadow_lift.formula: rgb * min(Y^(gamma - 1), max(1, 1 / max(r, g, b))) where Y = clamp(dot(luma, rgb), 1e-6, 1); scale is 1 when Y >= 1; the cap keeps every channel at or below 1
shadow_lift.inherent: a profile's 'shadow_gamma' (1 = none) is always applied to that animal's view; the effective gamma is min(user gamma, shadow_gamma), i.e. the stronger lift, never stacked
